sources.title: How do I build a simple text link to a specific item on Amazon?
sources.quote: "So if you need to build a simple text link to a specific item on Amazon.com, here is the link format you need to use: http://www.amazon.com/dp/ASIN/ref=nosim?tag=YOURASSOCIATEID … This link format qualifies for the direct link bonus." On the ASIN: "ASIN is the 10-digit code that Amazon uses to denote specific products. It is short for 'Amazon.com Standard Item Number.' Every item in our catalog has a unique ASIN." On the identifier: "YOURASSOCIATEID is the unique ID that is used to identify your Associates account, automatically generated when you apply for the Associates Programme."
used_for: the ASIN definition the product-intent record measures each supplied token against
the tag slot the submitted tracking ID would occupy

sources.title: Associates Program — Application Review Process
sources.quote: "After you sign up, our Associates team will check your application once you've driven qualified sales (we require at least three within the first 180 days). Please note that personal orders do not qualify." … "All Sites must have robust original content (even when advertising is removed) – a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts." … "Content on your website must be recent (generally within the last 60 days)." … and on the tag itself: "Associates special links are the identifiers (e.g. abcd-20) embedded in Amazon product links. These tags must be embedded in your Amazon product links on the site(s) declared in your application."
used_for: the published shape of a special-link tag, which the submitted tracking ID matches

sources.title: Why do I have to identify myself as an Associate? How should I do this on social media?
sources.quote: "To meet the Associate Program's requirements, you must (1) include a legally compliant disclosure with your links and (2) identify yourself on your Site as an Amazon Associate with the language required by the Operating Agreement." … "the Operating Agreement requires that the following statement clearly and conspicuously appears on your Site: 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.'" … a link-level disclosure must be "Clear" and "Conspicuous … placed near any affiliate link or product review in a location that customers will notice easily. They shouldn't have to hunt for it."

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google (rel="sponsored")
sources.quote: "Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value." Multiple values are permitted: "You may specify multiple rel values as a space- or comma-separated list."

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search — site reputation policy, human-review factors
sources.quote: On what a human review looks at: "How the content is presented, meaning are the graphic design, formatting, typography and UX features of the content consistent with the host domain? … The quality of the content … Its stated or implied authorship, meaning, is there an explicit acknowledgement of ownership or responsibility for the content? … Does the content appear on multiple other sites in identical or near-identical form". And the worked example of what draws action: "Likely to take action: unauthored affiliate article not integrated in publication … Neither the author of the article nor the responsible editor is identified, nor are there disclaimers about the commercial character of the content. The article isn't part of any of the thematic sections of the publication, and no links or menu are available to reach the article from the main page."
